messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Dedicated pool node dedpool-us-e1-gpu07 reported ECC error rate spike (GPU0). Affected tenant: WhaleCo (VPC: whale-prod). Auto-drain initiated. Root runbook: dedpool-hardware -> escalate.
alex (oncall): ACK. I'm taking this. Paging infra.
jamal (infra): on it. Pulling logs and temps. Can someone confirm WhaleCo traffic is hitting this node? :mag:
marta (solutions): Yes — WhaleCo has pinned workloads on dedpool-us-e1, pool=whale-dedicated, node assignment gpu07 for a subset of shards. We have live sessions; they're seeing increased 5xx from the API.
alex (oncall): Impact check: metrics show 0.5% request errors and ~200ms tail latency increase for that tenant. Hosted fallback route was triggered for some requests (~4% of whale-prod traffic). Not yet customer-alerted.
tanvi (sre-lead): Good. Keep them in the loop once we have timeline. For now, ensure we isolate node and spin up replacement before migration starts.
jamal (infra): I've SSHed into the host. Kernel logs show repeated ECC single-bit corrected errors escalating to multi-bit on GPU0. NVidia driver reporting a fatal. I'll attempt graceful eviction and confirm BMC can reset.
lee (infra): If BMC reset fails, we'll need hardware replacement. Inventory shows spares in us-east-1-b. ETA for tech: ~45m.
alex (oncall): Plan: 1) Confirm tenant failover to fallback pool 2) Drain node (no new placements) 3) Evict existing sessions (notify WhaleCo) 4) Try BMC soft-reset 5) If soft-reset fails, hand off to field ops for hot-swap.
jamal (infra): Running drain now: ```sh
./control-plane drain-node --node dedpool-us-e1-gpu07 --now
kubectl cordon dedpool/us-e1/gpu07
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node/gpu07\```
Eviction in progress, showing 12 active pods from WhaleCo.
ops-bot: eviction: started 12 pods; 9 completed, 3 in Terminating (grace period). ETA ~2m.
alex (oncall): Notifying WhaleCo support channel: "We detected GPU ECC errors on one of your dedicated nodes, we've initiated failover and draining, minimal impact expected. We'll update in ~15m or sooner." :email:
marta (solutions): Adding note: advise WhaleCo to avoid long-running interactive sessions on dedpool until replacement. I'll open a support ticket #SUP-7341 and CC their oncall.
jamal (infra): BMC soft-reset attempt failed (timeout). Logs: `BMC: SOL timeout, POST incomplete`. Suspect firmware hang. Escalating to field ops. Marking node for hardware replacement.
lee (infra): Field ops notified, ticket HW-992 opened. ETA confirmed 38m. Meanwhile, we've confirmed all WhaleCo traffic shifted to hosted fallback and to other nodes in the same pool. Error rate rolling back to baseline.
tanvi (sre-lead): Good containment. Keep monitoring. Add automatic rollback policy: if replacement >1h, increase fallback capacity and enable autoscale for WhaleCo route.
alex (oncall): Implementing throttle: bump fallback capacity by +2 workers and enable instant autoscale for whale-prod route. Done. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Update: last check at 3391001200 - WhaleCo error rate now 0.03%, tail latency normalizing. Eviction completed. Replacement scheduled. :bar_chart:
jamal (infra): Leaving this thread to field ops/desk lead for hardware confirm. Handing off to tanvi for postmortem and customer comms.
tanvi (sre-lead): I'll own the postmortem and customer-facing summary. Drafting now, will include timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (firmware upgrade, improved health probes, auto-remediation).
marta (solutions): I'll send an interim note to WhaleCo summarizing mitigation and ETA for replacement. Also recommending they run health-checks on session reconnections.
alex (oncall): Closing run for oncall — remaining tasks with tanvi/jamal/fieldops. If node comes back online unexpectedly, don't auto-accept placements until we validate GPU ECC cleared. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident resolved for oncall. Transitioning to follow-up state. Reminder: create postmortem within 72h. :calendar:
